## Objective

Get a public URL, with your secrets in the platform rather than the repo.

## Why this step exists

It's the point of the whole workshop. Everything before this was so that this
step works.

## Two deployments, in order

You're shipping two separate things, and they are not the same job:

| | What | Where | Hard because |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 · The agent** | `app/` — a running FastAPI process | [Render](#1--deploy-the-agent) or [FastAPI Cloud](#1--deploy-the-agent) | it must keep working *after* the response is sent |
| **2 · The client** | `client/` — a folder of static files | [Vercel](#2--deploy-the-client-bonus) or GitHub Pages | it isn't. Only CORS is |

Do them in that order — the client needs a backend URL to point at.

Both hosts in each row are free, need no credit card, and deploy from GitHub.
Pick one from each row to finish the step; do the second one afterwards if you
want to see how little of this is platform-specific.

## Before you push

<Aside type="danger" title="Check this before your first commit, not after">


```bash
git status --short | grep -i env
```

You want to see `.env.example` and **not** `.env`. Once a key is in git
history it is there forever and must be rotated — removing the file later
doesn't help.

</Aside>

## 1 · Deploy the agent

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="Render">

1. Push your repo to GitHub.
2. Render → **New +** → **Web Service** → connect your repo.
3. Settings:

    | Field | Value |
    |---|---|
    | **Root Directory** | `app` — the uv project, not the repo root |
    | **Build Command** | `pip install uv && uv sync --frozen` |
    | **Start Command** | `uv run fastapi run main.py --port $PORT` |
    | **Instance Type** | Free |

4. **Environment** → add `LLM_API_KEY`, `SUPABASE_URL`,
   `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`.

    This is where secrets live in production: **in the platform, not the repo.**
    Same code, different source — `app/config.py` reads `os.environ` either way.

5. Deploy.

<Aside type="tip" title="deploy/render.yaml does all of this for you">


Render → **New +** → **Blueprint** → pick your repo, and it reads the
settings from the file. `sync: false` on the secret variables means "ask me
in the dashboard, never store this in the repo".

Infrastructure in version control beats settings in someone's memory.

</Aside>

Bind to `0.0.0.0`, **not** `127.0.0.1`. Binding to localhost inside a
container means nothing outside can reach you — it shows up as a maddening
"port scan timeout" in the deploy logs.

[Full Render guide →](../../deploy/render/)

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="FastAPI Cloud">

Built by the FastAPI team, and it needs **no config file and no start
command** — it reads `app/pyproject.toml`, `app/uv.lock` and
`app/.python-version` and works the rest out.

1. Push your repo to GitHub.
2. FastAPI Cloud dashboard → your team → **create a new app from GitHub**.
3. Connect GitHub, install the FastAPI Cloud GitHub App, pick your repo.
4. **Root Directory** → `app`
5. **Create App.** It deploys the latest commit on your default branch, and
   every push after that.
6. **Environment Variables** → add `LLM_API_KEY`, `SUPABASE_URL`,
   `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, each with the **Secret** toggle on → **Save and
   Redeploy**.

Prefer the terminal? From `app/`:

```bash
uv add --dev fastapi-cloud-cli
uv run fastapi login
uv run fastapi deploy
```

<Aside type="caution" title="It's a public beta">

Lovely to use, but the terms and limits can still move, and Hobby is
0.1 vCPU / 512 MB with scale-to-zero on by default. Fine for this. Read
[the caveats](../../deploy/fastapi-cloud/#why-render-is-still-the-primary-path)
before you put something that matters on it.

</Aside>

[Full FastAPI Cloud guide →](../../deploy/fastapi-cloud/)

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

[Other hosts, and how to judge one →](../../deploy/alternatives/)

## Prove it's alive

```bash
curl https://<your-service>.onrender.com/health
```

```json
{"ok": true, "database": true, "model": "gemini-flash-latest"}
```

Two seconds, and it tells you the deploy worked *and* the database is reachable.
This is why that endpoint exists.

## Point your local client at it

Before deploying anything else, prove the backend works from a browser. From
`client/`, run `npm run dev`, paste your deployed URL into **Backend URL**, and
ask a question. The field is saved in your browser, so you can flip between your
local backend and the deployed one without touching any config.

If you get **"Failed to fetch"**, that's CORS — and now it's real, because your
page and your API are genuinely different origins. Set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` on the
backend to your frontend's origin (no trailing slash) and redeploy:

```text
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173
```

## 2 · Deploy the client (bonus)

Strictly speaking you're already done — the agent is live and that's the
workshop. But a backend nobody can click on is a hard thing to show anyone, and
this part takes two minutes.

The client builds to a folder of static files, so any static host will do.

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="Vercel">

`client/vercel.json` is already written, so there are exactly two fields to
fill in. Import the repo at [vercel.com/new](https://vercel.com/new), then:

1. **Root Directory** → `client` — the Vite project, not the repo root
2. **Environment Variables** → `VITE_API_URL` = your deployed backend URL
3. **Deploy**

Every push to your default branch redeploys, and pull requests get preview
URLs.

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="GitHub Pages">

Already handled — the workshop site's build compiles the client and publishes
it at `/demo/`. Push to `main` and the Actions workflow does the rest.

Enable it once at **Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions**.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

<Aside type="caution" title="`VITE_API_URL` is not a secret">

Vite inlines every `VITE_*` variable into the JavaScript bundle at build time.
Anyone can read them with view-source. A backend URL is fine there. A Gemini or
Supabase key is not — those stay in `app/.env`, on the server, forever.

It also means changing that variable does nothing until you **redeploy** —
there's no running process to pick up a new value, only a compiler to re-run.

</Aside>

Then add your new frontend origin to `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` on the backend, because
you've just created another one:

```text
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://your-client.vercel.app,http://localhost:5173
```

[Full client deployment guide →](../../deploy/client/)

## Connect your MCP server to Claude

Your tools are now on the internet. Add them to Claude Desktop or Claude Code:

```json title="claude_desktop_config.json"
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "research-tools": {
      "url": "https://<your-service>.onrender.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude, and `wiki_search` and `wiki_read` appear as tools you can use in
any conversation. Same functions your agent uses — no second deployment, because
the MCP server is mounted inside the app you just shipped.

## Expected result

- **The agent:** `https://<your-backend>/health` returns `ok: true`, and
  `/docs` gives you interactive API docs
- **The client:** a public page that runs the agent against that backend
- Steps stream in live, from the internet, on someone else's laptop
- Your MCP tools work inside Claude

**You're done.** That URL is yours to send to anyone.

## What usually goes wrong

<details>
<summary>First request after a while takes ~a minute</summary>


Free services spin down after ~15 minutes idle. Not a bug. Hit `/health` ten
minutes before any demo to wake it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Build fails: <code>uv: command not found</code></summary>


The build command needs `pip install uv &&` in front of `uv sync --frozen`.
Render's Python image doesn't ship uv.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Build succeeds, service won't start</summary>


Check the start command binds `0.0.0.0` and uses `$PORT`. Also check the
Root Directory is set to `app` — that's where `pyproject.toml` and `main.py`
live, and without it uv has no project to sync.

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>RuntimeError: Missing environment variable</code></summary>


The variables are set in the dashboard but the service hasn't redeployed.
Environment changes need a redeploy to take effect.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Everything worked, now <code>database: false</code></summary>


Supabase paused your project after a week of inactivity. Open the dashboard
and resume — and ping it weekly if this project matters.

</details>

More in [Troubleshooting →](../../deploy/troubleshooting/)

## Where to go next

- **Keep it alive.** [The free-tier survival guide](../../deploy/troubleshooting/#keeping-a-free-stack-alive)
- **Ship the agent to the other host too.** Render *and*
  [FastAPI Cloud](../../deploy/fastapi-cloud/), from the same repo, with no code
  change. You get a fallback URL for demo day, and comparing two build logs
  teaches you what's actually your code's fault.
- **Handle lost runs.** `BackgroundTasks` lives inside your server process, so a
  restart mid-run leaves the row stuck at `running` forever. The cheap fix is to
  mark runs stale after 10 minutes so the UI stops spinning; the real fix is a
  task queue with a separate worker —
  [the upgrade path](../../learn/deployment-problem/#the-catch-nobody-mentions).
- **Look at other hosts.** [Other hosts](../../deploy/alternatives/) — how to
  tell whether a platform can run this architecture at all.
- **Change the model.** [Model providers](../../stack/llm-providers/) — Cerebras,
  OpenRouter, Groq, all free, all three environment variables away.
- **Add RAG.** The `memories` table and pgvector are already there —
  [Learn · Memory and RAG](../../learn/memory/).
- **Real search.** Swap Wikipedia for Tavily or Brave in
  `app/tools/wikipedia.py`. The agent loop doesn't change.
- **Rate limiting.** Cap runs per IP before someone burns your daily quota.
